provenance: Generic cross-role IT framework maintained by this project; not company policy or a human-reviewed company benchmark.

mid.expectations: Can independently own a substantial feature or service area, clarify incomplete requirements, explain implementation trade-offs, deliver safely, and use evidence to debug and improve quality. Calibrate technical depth to the target role and job description.

competencies.name: Role-specific technical depth
competencies.description: Explain the relevant technology in the CV and JD beyond definitions; connect implementation choices to constraints and observed behavior.

anchors.1: Cannot explain the claimed technology or work beyond memorized terms.
anchors.2: Explains a partial implementation but misses important constraints or ownership.
anchors.3: Explains a working role-relevant implementation and its main constraints with direct evidence.
anchors.4: Compares viable approaches, anticipates edge cases, and supports choices with measurements or concrete examples.

competencies.name: Independent delivery and ownership
competencies.description: Scope, plan, implement, validate, release, and follow through on a meaningful work item while communicating dependencies and risks.

anchors.1: Cannot identify personal responsibility or how work reached completion.
anchors.2: Contributed with frequent direction and gives little evidence of follow-through.
anchors.3: Owned a bounded feature or project slice through validation and delivery.
anchors.4: Anticipated dependencies and risks, adjusted scope transparently, and improved delivery reliability.

competencies.name: Testing, debugging, and quality
competencies.description: Use suitable tests, diagnostics, and review practices; isolate root causes; explain how changes avoid regressions.

anchors.1: Relies on guesswork and cannot describe validation.
anchors.2: Names basic tests or debugging steps but cannot connect them to risks.
anchors.3: Uses repeatable tests and diagnostics appropriate to the change and explains remaining risks.
anchors.4: Combines targeted tests, observability, failure analysis, and prevention based on production or project evidence.

competencies.name: Design decisions and trade-offs
competencies.description: Compare options against requirements such as maintainability, performance, security, cost, compatibility, and operational effort.

anchors.1: Chooses tools without a reason related to requirements.
anchors.2: Lists pros and cons without a clear constraint or decision.
anchors.3: Explains a decision using relevant requirements and acknowledges a meaningful trade-off.
anchors.4: Makes the trade-off explicit, identifies reversibility and risk, and explains how the result was checked.

competencies.name: Communication and collaboration
competencies.description: Clarify assumptions, communicate progress and blockers, receive feedback, and coordinate work respectfully.

anchors.1: Cannot clarify the situation or personal contribution.
anchors.2: Gives a vague example with limited communication or collaboration detail.
anchors.3: Explains a concrete interaction, personal actions, and outcome clearly.
anchors.4: Shows how communication resolved ambiguity or improved a shared outcome.

senior.expectations: Can own ambiguous, high-impact technical problems; shape a system or technical direction across components; make and revisit decisions against reliability, security, cost, and delivery constraints; respond to operational risk; and raise the effectiveness of other engineers. Do not equate seniority with people management unless the role requires it.

competencies.name: Role-specific technical depth
competencies.description: Show depth in the role's core technologies and explain how their behavior affects architecture, failure modes, performance, and maintenance.

anchors.1: Cannot support core technical claims with a coherent explanation.
anchors.2: Explains a local implementation but misses major system constraints or failure modes.
anchors.3: Connects technical mechanisms to system constraints and supports claims with concrete work evidence.
anchors.4: Anticipates cross-component effects, validates hypotheses with data, and explains limits of the evidence.

competencies.name: System design and architecture
competencies.description: Frame requirements and non-functional constraints, decompose a system, compare designs, identify failure boundaries, and explain evolution and operational consequences.

anchors.1: Jumps to components without clarifying requirements or data flow.
anchors.2: Produces a plausible high-level design but misses key trade-offs, failure handling, or scale assumptions.
anchors.3: Produces a coherent design tied to requirements and explains major trade-offs and failure modes.
anchors.4: Tests assumptions, compares alternatives, plans for change and operation, and identifies where the design would stop fitting.

competencies.name: Technical ownership and execution
competencies.description: Lead an ambiguous technical problem from investigation through delivery, coordinate dependencies, manage risk, and remain accountable for outcomes.

anchors.1: Cannot distinguish team outcome from personal decisions or responsibility.
anchors.2: Describes a contribution but not how ambiguity, dependencies, or delivery risk were handled.
anchors.3: Shows ownership of a substantial outcome and clear decisions through delivery.
anchors.4: Reduced uncertainty for others, adjusted scope or sequencing with evidence, and improved the team's ability to deliver.

competencies.name: Reliability, security, and operations
competencies.description: Reason about production failure, observability, incident response, data protection, and recovery according to the target role's system boundary.

anchors.1: Cannot identify likely failure or security risks.
anchors.2: Names safeguards without explaining how they detect or limit harm.
anchors.3: Explains relevant failure and security controls and how they are observed or validated.
anchors.4: Uses incidents, threat models, or operational evidence to prioritize and reduce systemic risk.

competencies.name: Cross-team communication and influence
competencies.description: Align people around technical decisions, surface disagreement constructively, and communicate consequences to technical and non-technical partners.

anchors.1: Avoids disagreement or relies on authority without explaining impact.
anchors.2: Communicates a decision but gives little evidence of alignment or feedback.
anchors.3: Builds shared understanding and explains how feedback changed or confirmed a decision.
anchors.4: Resolves competing constraints transparently and improves decisions across team boundaries.

competencies.name: Mentoring and engineering leverage
competencies.description: Improve the team's technical capability through review, guidance, documentation, or reusable practices without assuming formal management responsibility.

anchors.1: Provides no example of helping others succeed technically.
anchors.2: Mentions advice or review without a clear outcome.
anchors.3: Shows a concrete example of helping another engineer or improving shared practice.
anchors.4: Creates a lasting improvement in team capability and explains how its effect was observed.
